Find the area $A$ of the finite region enclosed between $y=-3{x}^{2}+8$ and $y=-{x}^{2},$ shown above. Do not round the answer.

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*

$A=$ 
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to determine the limits of integration. To do this, we equate the two functions and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}^{2}+8 & =-{x}^{2} \\ -2{x}^{2}+8 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-4 & =0 \\ (x-2)(x+2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we need to integrate from $x=-2$ to $x=2.$

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273827/assets/336a1503663239debacda06ca200e47151493ffbc94c3b797afb274c3355db97.png)

The vertical line 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=-{x}^{2},$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=-3{x}^{2}+8.$

We can now set up the integration with our $x$ values (Top-Bottom):

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}[(-3{x}^{2}+8)-(-{x}^{2})\,]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}(-2{x}^{2}+8)\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}(8-2{x}^{2})\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the integrand is an even function. Therefore, we can find the area as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}(8-2{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{(8x-\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3})|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =2((8\cdot 2-\frac{2}{3}\cdot {2}^{3})-0) \\  & =2((16-\frac{16}{3})-(0)) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{32}{3} \\  & =\frac{64}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
